column1: # Who drives the transform's angles. Cycle 1364.
# 0x822A2B50 builds the argument block whose +0x18 and +0x1C become two of the
# three angles 0x822A1E80 applies (cycles 1330, 1331). It has SIX call sites, in
# six functions, and none of them is a vtable slot -- FindDataPointersTo returns
# one .pdata row for each, which the tool labels.
# columns: call_site function f1 f2 f3
0x822ECBE8
0x822ED2F8
# sub_822A2C80 IS THE UNIT'S OWN VTABLE SLOT +0x44 (cycle 1337, one of the two
# transform entry points a CAce6Unit exposes). It passes ONE incoming float three
# times, so on that path all three rotations take the same angle.
# Four of the six take their target object as [[0x826E4EB4] + rN + 1028] -- from
# the context, at +0x404, indexed by a register.
# THE FINDING: not one of the six reads anything from the input command path.
# No 0x826EDB98, no command frame, no slot mask. The angles come from OBJECT
# FIELDS at +0x10/+0x14, +0x14/+0x18 or +0x24, or from a register the caller
# already held.
# So something between the input tick and the transform writes those fields, and
# it is neither of the two ends this campaign has mapped: the tick is five
# contracted behaviours and every float in it is a timer (cycle 1363), and the
# transform is contracted as retail_transform (cycle 1328).
# NOT ESTABLISHED: what writes obj+0x10 and obj+0x14 for sub_822A2BE8's object;
# what the four context-sourced objects are; what sub_822A2C80's single float is.
